title: What Is the Best Carpet for Stairs? Durability, Safety and Style
meta: The best carpet for stairs is a dense, low-pile nylon cut pile over a thin, firm pad. Wills Flooring covers durability, safety and style for Lynnwood stairs.
keywords: best carpet for stairs, carpet for stairs durability, stair carpet Lynnwood WA, waterfall vs Hollywood stair carpet, best carpet pad for stairs, Berber on stairs

blocks.lead: The best carpet for stairs is a dense, low-pile cut carpet in solution-dyed nylon, installed over a thin, firm pad and wrapped tight at every nosing.
blocks.detail: Stairs wear out three to five times faster than any room in the house because every foot lands on the same three inches of each tread. Fiber resilience, pile density and a pad that does not flex are what keep a staircase looking new. Thick, soft and loopy are the three words to avoid.

blocks.html: Lynnwood is a staircase town. The split-levels and tri-levels built in Alderwood, Meadowdale and Martha Lake between the 1960s and 1980s have two short flights that every trip to the kitchen crosses, and the new townhomes going up near the light rail station stack three stories of stairs. So when a Lynnwood homeowner asks us which carpet to use on the stairs, the honest answer is: the toughest one in the house, chosen differently from the bedroom carpet, even if it is the same color.

blocks.text: Durability: why stairs give out first

items.title: The nosing takes every step
items.text: On a flat floor, traffic spreads across a hallway. On a stair, every foot lands on the front edge of the tread and pushes the pile forward over the nosing. That edge is where the backing shows first. The fix is a carpet whose fibers spring back, not one that feels soft in the store.

items.title: Nylon resilience wins
items.text: Solution-dyed nylon 6,6 recovers from crushing better than polyester, triexta or olefin. On a bedroom floor the difference takes a decade to show. On the top three treads of a Lynnwood split-level it shows in two years. Triexta is a fair second choice; polyester is not.

items.title: Density over thickness
items.text: Push your thumb into the sample. If you can feel the backing easily, the pile is too sparse for stairs. Look for a face weight around 40 oz and up, a tight twist and a pile height under half an inch. Short and dense outlasts tall and plush on a stair every time.

items.title: The pad is the hidden variable
items.text: A thick, cushy pad lets the carpet flex over the nosing with every step, which breaks down the backing and loosens the wrap. Stairs want a thin, dense pad, about 3/8 in at 8 lb density, so the carpet stays tight and the tread feels firm underfoot.

blocks.text: Safety: what actually keeps people upright

items.html: Low pile for sure footing. Deep pile rolls under the ball of the foot on the way down. A low, dense cut pile gives a flat, predictable surface, which matters for kids taking the stairs at a run and for anyone with a cane.

Tight installation. A stair carpet that has loosened at the nosing is the most common cause of stair falls we hear about. Every tread should be stretched and stapled or tacked so nothing shifts when you push it with your toe.

Contrast and pattern. Split-level stairwells are dim. A carpet with a subtle pattern or a tone that contrasts with the walls helps the eye read each tread edge. Solid, high-sheen carpets hide the edges and cause missteps.
Runners need grip. A runner over the original oak treads looks great in older Lynnwood ramblers, but it must be fastened at every step with rods or staples, never laid loose.
Fix squeaks and loose treads first. We screw down loose treads and shim risers before a single piece of carpet goes on. A squeak you can hear becomes a wobble you can feel once the carpet hides it.

blocks.text: Same carpet everywhere, or a tougher grade on the stairs?

a.title: Choose this when
items: The carpet you love for the bedrooms already meets the stair spec: dense nylon, low pile
You want the hallway and stairs to read as one surface
The staircase is short and lightly used, such as a two-step landing
You may sell within a few years and want a clean, uniform look

b.title: Choose this when
items: The bedroom carpet is a softer polyester or a plush you chose for comfort
Kids, dogs and a main flight everyone uses ten times a day
A three-story townhome where the stairs carry all the traffic
You want the bedrooms cheaper and the stairs to last as long as they do

blocks.title: A Reddit question we get in person too:
blocks.text: "Can I just use the leftover bedroom carpet on the stairs?" Only if it passes the thumb test and is a cut pile. Otherwise the bedrooms will look new in five years while the stairs look ten years old, and you will replace the stairs alone, which is the most expensive way to buy carpet.
Mistakes we fix on Lynnwood staircases

items.html: Berber and loop pile on stairs. Loops snag on shoes, claws and vacuums, and the tight backing does not bend cleanly around a nosing. The frayed edge that results cannot be repaired.
Thick pad from the bedrooms carried onto the stairs. The carpet flexes, the wrap loosens and the nosing wears through early. Stairs get their own pad.
Seams on a tread. Each tread should be one piece. A seam on a stair opens under foot traffic within a year.
Loose waterfall wraps. A waterfall that is not stapled under the nosing sags into a trip hazard. It has to be tight on day one.

Skipping the count. Stairs are quoted per tread, and a landing counts. We measure every step at the free estimate so the written price is the final price. See our carpet installation page for what is included.

faq.q: Is Berber carpet okay on stairs?
faq.a: We advise against it. Loop-pile carpets snag on shoes, pet claws and vacuum heads, and a pulled loop on a stair runs across the whole tread. The stiff backing also resists wrapping around the nosing cleanly. A dense low cut pile in the same color gives you the Berber look without the failures.

faq.q: What pile height is best for stairs?
faq.a: Under half an inch, and the denser the better. Low pile keeps the foot flat and stable on the way down, wraps tightly around the nosing and hides less dirt in the fibers. Tall plush and shag both roll under the foot and wear through at the tread edge quickly.

Yes, but a different pad than the rooms. Stairs want a thin, dense pad around 3/8 inch at 8 lb density so the carpet stays firm and tight at the nosing. A thick, soft pad on stairs lets the carpet flex, loosens the wrap and shortens carpet life.

faq.q: How long does carpet last on stairs?
faq.a: A dense solution-dyed nylon installed tight over a firm pad typically lasts 10 years or more on a busy Lynnwood staircase. A builder-grade polyester on the same flight can show backing at the nosing in three to five years. Fiber and density matter more on stairs than anywhere else in the house.

faq.q: Waterfall or Hollywood: which is better?
faq.a: Hollywood, also called cap and band, wraps each nosing tightly and looks tailored on open or bullnose stairs. Waterfall drapes straight down and suits closed flights and thicker carpets. Hollywood takes more labor per stair. Both are safe when installed tight; neither is inherently more durable.

faq.q: Can I put a carpet runner over hardwood stairs?
faq.a: Yes, and it is a good look in older Lynnwood ramblers with original oak or fir treads. The runner must be fastened at every tread with staples or rods, never laid loose. If the exposed wood is worn, refinish the treads before the runner goes down, since it is hard to do afterward.
